context:
Goal: no leftover browser processes keep running in the coordinator's cloud machine.
Problem (rule): twelve headless Chrome processes from a finished designer are still running (pids 23961, 23969, 23970, 23993, 23996, 24010, 24044, 24056, 24058, 24082, 24084, 24106); the coordinator's stop was refused by the guard against machine-wide kills, and only your typed override lets it through.
Based on (ruling): you said at 13:30 CST on 2026-11-21 that leftover Chrome can end (passed by the coordinator at 13:54 CST).
Departs from: main refuses a stop of processes the session did not start — this allows stopping these twelve, once.
Waiting on: your typed override in the coordinator's session; the coordinator does nothing further meanwhile.

options.gain: The twelve processes end and stop using the machine.
options.how: You type override in the coordinator's session; the coordinator stops only these twelve pids.
options.label: Yes, stop these twelve
options.lose: If a process were still in use, it would end too (the designer is finished).

options.gain: Nothing ends that you did not approve one by one.
options.how: The processes keep running until the machine is reclaimed.
options.label: No, leave them
options.lose: Twelve idle processes keep using memory.

title: May the coordinator stop twelve leftover headless Chrome processes from a finished designer?
why: You already said leftover Chrome can end; only your typed override lets the stop through.
